title-proc.eng: NPHarvest recycled materials - from raw materials to end products

description-proc.eng: Introduction NPHarvest Ltd develops technologies for recovering nutrients from wastewaters, enabling the recycling of nitrogen and phosphorus back into productive use. NPHarvest’s solution is based on a hydrophobic membrane process for ammonia recovery and lime precipitation for phosphorus recovery. The end products of the recovery process are a liquid ammonium salt and solid amorphous calcium phosphate which has organic material mixed in the product. These are categorically raw materials rather than commercial products and further development is necessary. Project Description and Objectives The goal of this procurement is product development work aimed at transforming NPHarvest’s recovered nutrients — ammonium salt and calcium-P-material — into finished, market-ready products that can be but are not limited to fertilizers. The work includes in particular: - selection of a suitable ammonium salt - determination of other required nutrients and their optimal ratios, including not only nitrogen and phosphorus but also other nutrients such as potassium, sulfur, calcium, magnesium, and micronutrients, if necessary - identification of potential binding and additive substances, and - optimization of the final product form (e.g. pellets or granules, powder, or liquid) from recovered raw materials into refined end products. An important part of the project is to develop the end products with the nutrient recovery process in mind, ensuring that nutrients are recovered in forms that are as easily processable and usable as possible. At a broader level, the project contributes to advancing nutrient recycling. Although positive research results exist regarding the use of recycled fertilizers, such products have not yet reached the market at scale. NPHarvest aims to address the economic challenges of nutrient recovery by making both recovery processes and recycled nutrient products commercially viable. Economic viability is a prerequisite for the effective circulation of nutrients in society. Project Outcomes The outcomes of the project will include: - one to three products and what is required to produce them as part of the nutrient recovery process, - producing samples and usage guidelines for these products, and - the necessary technical and practical knowledge to support further product development, market entry, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

title-proc.eng: Wireless Communication

description-proc.eng: DSB has been given the responsibility to automate the S-network, i.e., to transform the S-Train system from a traditional urban railway to a fully automated (GoA4) transport system. To execute this responsibility, DSB has set up a programme to deliver and implement the new capabilities needed for automating the S-network – “The Future S-network Programme”. The Future S-network Programme will be implemented through a number of separate projects that together will provide the fundament for DSB’s intended future operational and maintenance model for a fully automated S-network. One of these projects is the acquisition of wireless data communication and related services. The wireless data communication services to be delivered under the contracts covered by this tender shall enable transmitting of audio and real-time data streams between the future S-trains and central system setup in DSB´s data centres. This tender covers three (3) contracts for wireless data communication and related services. The services covered by the three (3) contracts are identical. Three contracts are tendered in order to obtain redundancy. However, one (1) of the three (3) contracts is conditioned. Accordingly, the third contract can only be activated in case it is concluded that the Mobile Connectivity available to DSB by using two Mobile Networks is not sufficient for DSB’s intended operation of driverless S-trains. In the event that one supplier’s mobile network becomes unavailable, DSB must be able to switch to another supplier’s mobile network in order to ensure the stable operation of the new driverless trains. On this basis, DSB does not wish to enter into contracts for the supply of mobile data with more than one supplier that uses the same mobile network for the provision of mobile data services for the fulfilment of the contract. Two suppliers shall be deemed to use the same mobile network for the fulfilment of the contract if mobile network data services are delivered under the contract using the same underlying radio access network (RAN) or mobile core network infrastructure. In connection with the award of contracts under this procurement, DSB will therefore not award more than one contract to tenderers that based on the tenderers’ statement in the tender will utilize the same mobile network for the fulfillment of the contract, as set out above. If DSB receives more than one tender that will utilize the same mobile network, cf. above, only the tender with the lowest evaluation price will be eligible for award. Any other tenders from tenderers using the same mobile network will not be awarded a contract. This is also the case if the implication is that less than three contracts may be awarded. II) Main Services Each contract covers the following main services: A) Initial Services B) Continuing Services Ad main service A) Initial Services The Initial Services shall cover all services necessary for the supplier to be able to deliver mobile connectivity to DSB. This shall include • Installation of terminal equipment (e.g. PE router) at three locations in the Copenhagen area appointed by DSB. • Establishment of fixed network between the supplier’s network and DSB’s two data centres, and fixed network to DSB’s test lab. • Delivery of approximately 450 SIM cards. • Integration between the supplier’s IT service management tool and DSB’s IT service management tool for appointed ITIL processes. • RAM demonstration report and coverage report providing insight into the supplier’s services and network. title-proc.eng: Laser for pump-probe spectroscopy at SLS 2.0

description-proc.fra: Il s'agit d'un appel d'offres pour un système laser qui sera utilisé au synchrotron Swiss Light Source (SLS2.0) pour des expériences de pompage-sondage sur deux lignes de lumière distinctes, SuperXAS et Phoenix. Ces expériences, menées dans le même bâtiment, nécessitent que le laser soit mobile entre les deux lignes de lumière. Pour la spectroscopie pompe-sonde, le laser doit fournir des longueurs d'onde réglables couvrant la gamme de l'ultraviolet (UV) au proche infrarouge (proche IR). La durée de l'impulsion laser doit être plus courte que celle des impulsions de rayons X, ce qui nécessite des impulsions de l'ordre de quelques dizaines de picosecondes (ps) ou moins. Une excitation efficace des matériaux étudiés nécessite un taux de répétition élevé compris entre 40 et 131 kHz, associé à une énergie d'impulsion élevée.
description-proc.deu: Dies ist eine Ausschreibung für ein Lasersystem, welches an der Synchrotron Lichtquelle Schweiz (SLS 2.0) für Pump-Probe-Experimente an den zwei Strahllinien SuperXAS und Phoenix eingesetzt werden soll. Da diese Experimente im selben Gebäude durchgeführt werden, muss der Laser zwischen den beiden Strahllinien mobil sein. Für die Pump-Probe-Spektroskopie muss der Laser abstimmbare Wellenlängen im Ultraviolettbereich (UV) bis zum nahen Infrarotbereich (nahes IR) liefern. Die Laserpulsdauer muss kürzer sein als die Röntgenpulse, sodass Pulse im Bereich von einigen zehn Pikosekunden (ps) oder kürzer erforderlich sind. Eine effiziente Anregung der untersuchten Materialien erfordert eine hohe Wiederholungsrate im Bereich von 40–131 kHz in Kombination mit einer hohen Pulsenergie.
description-proc.eng: This is a call for tender for a laser system which will be utilized at the Swiss Light Source 2.0 (SLS 2.0) synchrotron for pump-probe experiments at two distinct beamlines, SuperXAS and Phoenix. These experiments, conducted within the same building, require the laser to be mobile between the two beamlines. For pump-probe spectroscopy, the laser is to provide tunable wavelengths spanning the ultraviolet (UV) to near-infrared (near-IR) range. The laser pulse duration needs to be shorter than the X-ray pulses, thus requiring pulses in the tens of picoseconds (ps) or shorter timescale regime. Efficient excitation of the studied materials necessitates a high repetition rate in the range 40-131 kHz combined with a high pulse energy.

description-proc.eng: Enterprise 2.0 Boosting Agriculture Market Access in Zambia is a EUR36 million matching grant facility co-financed by the European Union and the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ under the Climate-Resilient Agri-Food Systems (CREATE) programme. The overall objective of EZCF 2.0 is to catalyse a transformative shift in Zambia"s agri-food sector by increasing productivity, strengthening market access for smallholder farmers, and accelerating the adoption of sustainable, climate-smart, and inclusive production practices. The Action focuses on legumes and horticulture value chains, with geographic emphasis on four provinces linked to the Lobito Corridor. EZCF 2.0 mobilises private sector investment by providing matching grants to agribusinesses that demonstrate commercially viable, green, and inclusive business models. Supported enterprises are expected to integrate smallholder farmers into their value chains, create decent jobs, promote gender equality and youth inclusion, and adopt environmentally sustainable practices. Approximately 200,000 smallholder farmers, particularly women, young people, and vulnerable groups, are expected to benefit indirectly through improved market integration, incomes, and resilience to climate and economic shocks. The facility is implemented through two complementary grant schemes. Grant Scheme I (Growth and Scale Facility) provides medium and large matching grants (up to 1 Million Euro) to agribusinesses with high growth potential, using a competitive two-stage selection process supported by structured pre- and post-award technical assistance. Grant Scheme II (Micro-Grants Facility with ticket sizes between 10,000 and 50,000 Euro) targets smaller, indigenous enterprises through simplified procedures tailored to their scale and capacity and is implemented through a separate delivery partner. Beyond grant financing, EZCF 2.0 embeds comprehensive capacity development and technical assistance throughout the investment lifecycle. This includes pipeline development, application support, business and investment readiness, inclusive business model design, facilitation of linkages to financial institutions, and post-award strategic advisory services. Through these measures, the Action supports agribusinesses in accessing follow-on financing and strengthening their long-term financial sustainability beyond grant funding. Through its integrated approach, Enterprise 2.0 strengthens Zambia"s agribusiness ecosystem, leverages private capital, and contributes to green growth, food and nutrition security, and inclusive economic development.
